claims.text: Thermal exposure transforms metastable Mg-rich solid-solution regions into stable intermetallic compounds.
The transformation produces localized Mg depletion.
Thermal exposure promotes a discontinuous, porous MgO-rich surface phase.
A heterogeneous oxide scale and altered surface composition degrade high-temperature oxidation resistance.
A heterogeneous oxide scale and altered surface composition degrade aqueous corrosion behavior relative to the initial metastable state.
The proposed as-cast alloy has a relatively homogeneous distribution of metastable Mg-rich solid solution and finely dispersed intermetallic compounds.
The proposed alloy has an overall density below 6 g/cm³.
An oxidizing treatment at approximately 600–1000 °C will promote phase transformation and oxidation relative to an inert-atmosphere treatment.
Selective oxidation of Mg is coupled to the conversion of metastable Mg-rich zones into stable intermetallic compounds.
Mg oxidizes faster than the other alloy constituents because of its high reactivity.
Selective Mg oxidation depletes Mg from the matrix.
Mg depletion stabilizes intermetallic phases that are less corrosion resistant.
Rapid MgO formation does not produce a uniform, adherent protective scale.
Oxidizing thermal treatment will increase the volume fraction of stable intermetallic compounds relative to the as-cast baseline.
Oxidizing thermal treatment will measurably deplete Mg in near-surface regions.
Oxidizing thermal treatment will produce a porous or discontinuous MgO-rich scale.
Oxidizing thermal treatment will increase corrosion current density relative to the as-cast baseline.
Oxidizing thermal treatment will reduce high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to the as-cast baseline.
The as-cast baseline has no preformed oxide scale.
Changes in alloying elements or processing methods may produce different transformation pathways.
